problems.form_value: Dyads accepted 32.91 percent of AI-generated uses (40.90 percent excluding already-written and no-time answers), and about half of the entered answers were AI-generated (Table 5, p. 12).
problems.source_says: Minor locator error. The numbers are right, but Table 5 on p. 12 does not print 40.90 percent. Table 5 prints 32.91 percent accepted and 49.96 percent AI-generated entered answers. The 40.90 percent figure appears only in the Section 5.3 text on p. 11. The Table 5 averages give a different value, 7.60 / (23.10 - 0.73 - 3.24) = 39.73 percent, so an auditor can neither find nor derive 40.90 from the table. Suggested locator: 'p. 11, Section 5.3 (40.90 percent); Table 5, p. 12 (32.91 and 49.96 percent)'. No coded value changes.
problems.quote: Excluding uses that the dyads had already imagined on their own, and uses that they had no more time to enter from the total, this percentage rises to 40.90%
problems.locator: p. 11, Section 5.3, right column; p. 12, Table 5

confirmed.statement: (a) The document states random assignment twice: 'Upon arriving at the study location, dyads were randomly assigned to their experimental condition' and 'Because dyads were randomly assigned to experimental conditions, we did not control the distribution of demographic characteristics'. The form's assignment quote is verbatim and its locator is right.

Caveats that do not contradict the stated random assignment: the paper does not say how it randomized (coin, software, or blocks). The valid sample splits exactly 26 vs 26 dyads, and the arms differ in age (U = 1038.5, p = 0.038) and in private AI use (U = 1631.0, p = 0.040). The authors report no confounding effects in correlation and moderation checks.

Unit team and structure between are right. Dyads, not individuals, were assigned, and each dyad stayed in one condition. Two students booked each slot together before assignment, so dyads formed themselves.

(b) What was assigned is access to a generative-AI tool for the dyad's own work. AI-condition dyads could ask ChatGPT-4 for solutions in a chat window of the AUT interface, and the authors scored the answers each dyad entered. No condition differs only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.2.2; p. 6, Section 4.4.1; p. 7, Section 4.5.1

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is a large language model. The paper calls ChatGPT-4 'an off-the-shelf generative AI chatbot' and cites ChatGPT as Large-Language-Model-powered technology. Reference [80] reads 'Model: gpt-4, version: March 2024', and the Methods give no version, as the form says.
confirmed.locator: p. 1, Section 1; p. 4, Section 3; p. 16, reference [80]

confirmed.statement: Role open_chat fits. The design is user-led, with 'full human autonomy over AI usage'. The research team did no prompt engineering and chose not to restrict the AI. Copy-paste from the chat window into the AUT submission window was blocked, as the form says.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 3; p. 5, Section 4.2.2; p. 14, Section 7

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm matches the form: 'the control non-AI group performed the tasks without it', on the same three objects (fork, flower pot, suitcase) at four minutes each. Arm ai = none and comparison_type ai_vs_bau are right. Neither group had ChatGPT-4 in the immediate or the retention post-test, so the after_ai contrasts compare the two former arms.
confirmed.locator: pp. 4-5, Section 4.2; p. 5, Section 4.2.2 and Figure 1; p. 6, Sections 4.2.3 and 4.2.4

confirmed.statement: (e) Not applicable. AI access varies only between dyads, and the design has no within-person AI manipulation, so no order of conditions needs randomizing.

Arms n_analyzed = 52 people each and n_randomized = null are right. The paper reports only the valid sample (26 dyads/52 participants per condition) after a German-language inclusion rule and never gives the number of dyads randomized. The design summary's 'Fifty-two dyads ... were randomly assigned' describes the analyzed dyads, not a stated randomized count.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.2.1; p. 6, Section 4.3 and footnote 3

confirmed.statement: Preregistration on AsPredicted (https://aspredicted.org/msym-tbc2.pdf) is stated, as the form says.

The other arm and ai_tool details check out: four minutes per item, a shared large display, ChatGPT-4 removed for both post-tests, 32.91 percent of AI answers accepted, and 49.96 percent of entered answers AI-generated.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.2.2; p. 6, Sections 4.2.3 and 4.2.4; p. 12, Table 5

confirmed.statement: S2 (pre-study, 10 chatbots vs 20 human dyads) is correctly coded randomized = no. No person was assigned anything.

summary: The paper states twice that dyads were randomly assigned on arrival to off-the-shelf ChatGPT-4 in a chat window or to no AI on the AUT, and the form's assignment, unit, structure, arms, comparison type, and tool coding all match the text (pp. 4-6). The only error is a locator in ai_tool.how_used: the 40.90 percent acceptance figure is in the p. 11 text, not in Table 5 on p. 12, so criterion 1 holds.
